Joined by the term orders, a reading: High-Performance Order Storage 'introduces dedicated tables for data like orders and order addresses' (WC-S-0631), the store's orders that Shopify's Orders (SH-S-1507) and Salla's Orders (SA-S-1691) manage. Strained: it is how the orders are stored in the store's database, not their management in the admin. No capability of the model is order storage, and HPOS has no place of its own in the statements held beyond a released feature (WC-S-0630, WC-I-0355) and its option woocommerce_custom_orders_table_enabled (WC-S-5369), so by the dry run's test it isn't made a capability. Its reason, that WooCommerce 'traditionally stored store orders ... as custom WordPress post types or post meta records' (WC-S-0629), is cited under WC-C-032's key in domain A's CM-TRU-014, where the store's data is stored; scope.tsv names G under also. The reviewer may split or move it.
